subject.title: feat: let plugins control inbound debounce policy

question: Should OpenClaw expose the generic `inbound_debounce` plugin hook proposed here, prefer the WhatsApp conversation-config surface in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100970, or defer both approaches?
rationale: Both approaches solve the same operator need but create different permanent contracts: this PR expands the public plugin SDK and delivery path, while the alternative expands user configuration. Repository policy favors plugins over additional config when the API boundary is sound, but only maintainers can select the supported product contract.

options.title: Approve the plugin hook
options.body: Adopt the bounded first-explicit-decision hook, require live installed-plugin WhatsApp proof, and document that WhatsApp is currently its only caller.

options.title: Prefer conversation configuration
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100970 as the product surface and close this PR once that path is proven viable and selected.

options.title: Defer customization
options.body: Keep existing channel/account debounce behavior and close both proposals until a broader cross-channel contract is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Approve the plugin hook
recommendation.body: Adopt the bounded first-explicit-decision hook, require live installed-plugin WhatsApp proof, and document that WhatsApp is currently its only caller.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the visible reviewer previously involved in rejecting the earlier WhatsApp debounce direction and were directly asked to assess this revised contract.
